prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1305; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Officers responded to a side-impact collision at an intersection in Pasadena, Texas. Driver 1 was traveling through the intersection when the front of Driver 2's vehicle struck the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 reported shoulder pain, and the nature of the impact is consistent with that complaint. A Passenger was also seated in Driver 1's vehicle, and both the responding officer and the parties on scene confirmed that Passenger's presence at the time of the crash. Scene photographs show the damage is largely consistent with the described impact, and they document the positions of both vehicles. A few older scratches on the side panels may predate this collision and were noted but not attributed to it. No independent witnesses came forward. Driver 1 identified the driver as a household member who lives with the policyholder. Officers did not observe any traffic signal violations by either driver and issued no citations at the scene. Further review of the photographs and statements is recommended.
